$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Appearance section's Agent Chat rows, agentPane.display.* (cx-d5b5d). scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants from it (its docstring is the row format); schemas/settings/settings-schema.json is still exported from Swift and must not change when rows move here.

lists.name: agentPaneDisplay
lists.note: The agent chat's look (plans/cmux-next/chat-display-settings-DESIGN.md): the chat page reads the same names and ranges (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/chatDisplay.ts CHAT_DISPLAY), and its ... menu's Text & Width popover writes them. The font, code font and code size have no value of their own by default: the chat then follows the Markdown viewer's, and code follows the terminal font. Sizes and width never follow the viewer.

rows.note: The chat column's cap in points.

help.text: The widest the chat's column gets. On a wider pane the chat stays centered.
The chat fills the whole pane instead of the text width.

rows.note: The VS Code-style picture of the whole chat at its right edge (webviews chatMinimap/ChatMinimap.tsx). Off by default; the thread rail at the left (Toggle Thread Minimap) is its own thing.

help.text: A small picture of the whole chat at its right edge. Click or drag it to scroll.

rows.note: Taste prototype: the chat header's title as one monospace slash path, repo / branch / chat title (webviews header/ThreadTitle.tsx). Off by default; off, the header shows the plain title as before.

help.text: Show the chat's repository and branch before its title in the header, as a path.

rows.note: A taste prototype (Taste Board #19, winner and finalist list rows): a small status pill (Running, Needs you, Done, Failed) at the end of each live chat's row in All Chats (webviews newtab/AllChatsList.tsx ChatStatusPill), from the state the row already has; idle and indexed rows show none. Off by default: the rows are as before.

help.text: Shows Running, Needs you, Done or Failed as a small pill on each live chat in All Chats.

rows.note: A subagent's own pane says whose it is, "Subagent of <chat>" muted beside its name on the header's one line (webviews subagents/subagentPanes.ts paneHeading; Leo, 2026-11-22). Off by default; off, the header names the subagent alone, as before.

help.text: In a subagent's own pane, show which chat it belongs to beside its name in the header.

rows.note: A floating card at the chat's top right (webviews session-info/EnvironmentCard.tsx), after the Codex app's Environment panel: the chat folder's changes (Session Info's Changes row, changeCounts.ts), its branch or worktree, Commit or push (the diff tab's Commit form and Push, as the palette's Commit opens it) and Create PR (git.pullRequest). Off by default: today's chat draws no card. A look turns it on (chameleon-codex).

help.text: A card at the chat's top right with its changes, branch, commit and pull request.

rows.note: A pill centered over the composer naming how many files the chat folder changed and their lines (webviews session-info/EnvironmentCard.tsx ChangesPill), after the Codex app's "1 file changed +2 -2"; a click opens the diff beside the chat. Off by default: today's chat draws no pill.

help.text: A pill over the composer with how many files the chat changed.

rows.note: A soft sound when a long turn ends, the chat's checks pass or its pull request merges (webviews finish/finishMoments.ts; the host's pane.finishSound plays it only while macOS plays user interface sound effects). Off by default (leo-workspace research/2026-10-26-delight.md rule 7).

help.text: A soft sound when a long turn ends, its checks pass or its pull request merges.

rows.note: A turn with little to hide (under three tool calls and five seconds) draws flat, its work in a one-line summary such as "4s · Ran 2 commands", instead of folding under "Worked for 4s". Off unless switched on: Leo, 2026-11-25: "why isn't there a toggle? there should be one." (webviews conversation/turns.ts foldsTurn, chatDisplay.ts COMPACT_SHORT_TURNS_KEY).

help.text: A short turn shows a one-line summary of what it did, instead of folding under Worked for.

rows.note: A sent prompt pops in and settles where it lands, Claude's own user-message entrance (conversation.css SEND-POP; Leo, 2026-11-22: "it does a little pop and settle"). Off unless switched on: Leo, 2026-11-22: "hm im not necessarily sure if people will be wanting to do the send pop by default". The page sets data-send-pop on its root when on (chatDisplay.ts).

help.text: A prompt you send pops in and settles where it lands, instead of appearing at once.

rows.note: A sent prompt scrolls to the top of the transcript with room below it for the reply, which fills in under it (cmux#56827, Leo: "sent message scrolls to top"). Off unless switched on: off, the view follows the bottom as before. The room is one term of conversation/roomUnder.ts (sendTop), read from chatDisplay.ts.

help.text: A prompt you send moves to the top of the chat, with room below it for the reply.

rows.note: The hat over the composer tucked away to a pull tab at the composer's top middle (webviews subagents/TrayPullTab.tsx; Leo, 2026-11-04: "what if you wanted to collapse that one line?"). The hat's own chevron and the tab write it too.

help.text: Hides the running work bar. Hover the top of the composer to bring it back.

rows.note: Where along the composer's top edge the hat's tuck chevron and its pull tab sit (webviews subagents/TrayPullTab.tsx; Leo, 2026-11-04: "I also wonder if we'd want the grabber/dogear/whatever design thing on maybe the left... or the right...").

help.text: Where the running tray's handle sits on top of the composer.

rows.note: How the floating unread banner shows at the transcript's top start while the "New" line is off screen (webviews conversation/SinceDivider.tsx UnreadBanner, design/transcript-overlays.md; Leo, 2026-11-10: "you can have the collapsed view. You can have the expanded view. You can have, like, right click to just hide it completely. You can right click to bring it back"). The banner's chevron and the right-click menus of the banner and the line write it.

help.text: A banner for new turns when you come back to a chat. Right-click it to hide it.

rows.name: senderIconLead
rows.note: A sender's icon (webviews subagents/SenderIcon.tsx, senderIconLook.ts): the model family's mark with a small badge in the session's own color (Leo, 2026-11-05: "you either have the model family be the big one or the small one, and then you have the, like, colored either robot symbol or the sort of, you know, the diamond symbol, which I kind of personally like"). Which of the two is big.

help.text: Which is big in a sender's icon: the model's mark or the session badge.

rows.name: senderIconBadge
rows.note: The small glyph in the session's color on a sender's icon (webviews subagents/SenderIcon.tsx); none draws the mark alone.

help.text: The small colored glyph on a sender's icon that tells sessions of one model family apart.

rows.name: senderIconCorner
rows.note: Where the badge sits on a sender's icon (webviews subagents/SenderIcon.tsx).

help.text: Where the small glyph sits on a sender's icon.

rows.name: uiFont
rows.note: The face of the whole chat (webviews .../chatUiFont.ts; Leo, 2026-11-05: "I haven't tried switching fonts in my own app yet. So we could just try some stuff like that"). The default is the macOS system font (Lawrence, 2026-11-07: "default fonts on cmux for everything should be macos default, not inter"); Inter, with its calculated tracking or stock, is a choice.

help.text: The font of the whole chat: replies, the composer, cards and menus.

rows.name: uiFamily
rows.note: A CSS family or comma stack, no quotes; when set it wins over agentPane.display.font.ui (webviews chatUiFont). A theme's font pack names its faces here and in agentPane.display.font.faces.

help.text: A font family or a comma list of them. When set, it replaces the Chat Interface Font.

rows.name: proseFamily
rows.note: The face of the agent's reply prose; when set it wins over agentPane.display.font.preset.

help.text: The font of the agent's replies. When set, it replaces the Chat Font.

rows.name: faces
rows.note: Font files the chat page declares as @font-face: key = family, optionally suffixed :italic; value = file:PATH (absolute or at ~; in a theme file relative to the themes folder). At most 8 faces, each a plain woff2, woff, ttf or otf file of at most 2 MiB whose extension matches its bytes (cmux-config font_faces, Swift ChatFontFaces); the page gets each as a data:font URL.

help.text: A font file for each family, such as "Lora:italic": "file:~/Fonts/Lora-Italic.woff2".
Empty uses the Markdown viewer's code font.

rows.name: codeScale
rows.note: No value of its own by default: the chat follows markdown.code.scale; the placeholder is the Markdown viewer's default.

help.text: Code as a share of the chat's text size. Empty uses the Markdown viewer's.

rows.name: sessionInfoPlacement
rows.note: Where the chat's Session Info opens (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/SessionInfo.tsx). It was agentPane.display.inspector.placement (RenamedSettingKeys).

help.text: Push narrows the chat; Overlay covers it; Inline puts it atop the chat.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsEnvironment
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Environment section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: Where the chat runs: this Mac or Cloud, its folder and branch.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsContext
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Context section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: How full the context window is, and what fills it.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsSubagents
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Subagents section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The subagents and chats this chat started.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsTasks
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Background Tasks section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The commands, servers and scheduled jobs the chat runs.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsSources
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Sources section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The files and pages the agent read.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsOutputs
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Outputs section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The documents and files the chat made for you.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsChanges
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Pull Requests section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The chat's pull requests and their checks.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsUsage
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Usage section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: Tokens, cost and time this chat used.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsConnectors
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Connectors section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The MCP servers and connectors the chat has.

rows.name: sessionInfoShowsCarried
rows.note: Whether Session Info (the chat's thread details) shows its Carried memory section (webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/session-info/shownSections.ts). On by default: off, the section is not drawn at all.

help.text: The MCP servers and carried the chat has.

rows.name: environmentPlacement
rows.note: The machine and folder chip below the tab row (webviews/.../header/EnvironmentLine.tsx).

help.text: Where the chip sits: under the tabs (Left) or in the header (Right).

rows.note: What the chat's edge shows (webviews threadMinimap/ThreadMinimap.tsx): the prompt rail of ticks, the full map (ScrollMap.tsx), or nothing. The values are the thread-minimap-layout experiment's arms and the default is its default arm (webviews/test/thread-minimap-setting.test.ts checks both), so the row never says one thing while the chat shows another. The keywords are the words people search for it with (Leo, 2026-10-22, searching "TICK RAIL": "doesn't show as an option"). It was an on/off toggle; AgentPaneDisplaySettingsSchema.pageValue reads the old values.

help.text: What runs down the chat's edge.

rows.note: The chat detail ladder (webviews agent-session/acpmux/chatDetail.ts), one for the agent chat and Home Channels: a chat's ... menu changes its own level, and its "Make ... the default" writes this row. It replaces agentPane.display.presentation and agentPane.display.transcriptView, which still read: presentation messages is Messages, else the old transcript view carries over.

help.text: How much a chat shows: messages only, tool rows, thoughts, or every tool's output. A chat's ··· menu sets its own.

rows.page_hidden: legacy: agentPane.display.detail (Chat Detail) replaces it; the key still reads
rows.note: How much of each turn a chat shows (webviews conversation/transcriptView.ts), Claude Code desktop's Transcript view: a chat's ... menu changes its own, and its "Make ... the default" writes this row.

help.text: How much of each turn a chat shows. A chat's ··· menu sets its own.

rows.page_hidden: legacy: agentPane.display.detail (Chat Detail) replaces it; the key still reads

rows.note: A named look of the transcript (docs/cmux-next/transcript-customization.md): a bundle of look tokens from schemas/transcript-look/transcript-look.json. cmux sets no token, so it is the chat as it draws today.

help.text: How messages, cards and spacing look.

rows.note: Per-token overrides of the transcript look: an object of token name to value, each checked against schemas/transcript-look/transcript-look.json (cmux-config transcript_look; the page drops a value it refuses).

help.text: Token values that override the transcript look.

rows.page_hidden: an object of look tokens, edited in cmux-next.json or a theme file

rows.note: Prompt coach (webviews conversation/PromptCoachCard.tsx; Leo, 2026-11-08): after a chat in which the person corrected the agent three or more times before moving on, a card under that turn shows the chat's first prompt rewritten with what they added later, with Copy. Off: the chat asks acpmux for no rewrite (`_acpmux/prompt_coach`) and draws no card.

help.text: After a chat with many corrections, shows a better first prompt.

rows.name: statusVerbsMode
rows.note: The live line's short working verbs (webviews/.../statusVerbs.ts). Thinking is the default; Rotate opts into the per-turn -ing verbs and Custom reads the comma list.

help.text: Choose whether the live status line rotates through verbs or stays on Thinking.
Comma-separated -ing verbs for the live status line.

rows.name: thinkingShimmer
rows.note: How the live line's light band moves while the agent works (webviews agent chat). Cadenced is today's one-second sweep every four seconds; Continuous sweeps back to back, eased in and out, over shimmerPeriod.

help.text: How the light band moves across the live status line.

rows.name: thinkingShimmerPeriod
rows.note: One continuous shimmer pass in milliseconds; read only when shimmer is continuous.

help.text: How long one continuous pass of the shimmer takes.

rows.name: thinkingShimmerBand
rows.note: The shimmer band's width in points; 0 keeps today's band, half the line's width.

help.text: The width of the shimmer's light band. 0 uses half the line.

rows.name: thinkingJumpButton
rows.note: What Jump to latest shows while the agent works: the arrow (today), or three small dots in the theme accent moving in turn; the arrow comes back on hover and when the agent stops.

help.text: What the Jump to latest button shows while the agent works.

rows.name: thinkingGlyph
rows.note: A look's thinking dots: a cmux.particles/1 document (cmux-app-host js/ABI.md "Particles choreography", checked by the one Rust validator, cmux-app-host particles.rs, through cmux-config's domain:particles_document). The chat plays it before the live status line and, with jumpButton glyph, in Jump to latest, each choosing the document's trigger from the agent's current activity kind; a sidebar row plays it for cmux.sidebar.rows/1 indicator "glyph". A look may keep it in a file of its folder: {"$file": "thinking-glyph.json"} (cmux-customize setup::inline_files). Unset draws nothing new.

help.text: Dots a look plays while the agent works, as a cmux.particles/1 document.

rows.page_hidden: a cmux.particles/1 document a look or cmux settings set writes, edited in cmux-next.json

rows.name: thinkingGlyphSize
rows.note: The dot size in points Jump to latest draws the thinking glyph at, over the document's particle.size (the button is smaller than the status line); 0 keeps the document's size. The status line and sidebar rows always use the document's size.

help.text: The dot size of the thinking glyph in Jump to latest. 0 uses the glyph's own size.

rows.note: Whether the composer's model chip draws its provider's logo left of the model's name (webviews modelChipIcon.ts, cmux#38053). The chip's right-click writes it; the agent pages' storage ends with the launch, so the pick lives here.

help.text: Shows the provider's logo next to the model's name in the message box. Right-click the model to turn it off or on.

rows.note: The order of the model picker's harness tabs, as tab keys, first to last (webviews modelPickerOrder.ts). A drag of a tab on the picker's rail writes it; Starred always stays first, and a tab it does not name keeps its default place after the named ones. Empty: the default order. The agent pages' storage ends with the launch, so the order lives here.

help.text: The order of the harnesses in the model picker. Drag a harness in the picker to move it.

rows.page_hidden: tab keys, set by dragging a harness in the model picker

rows.note: What a click on the composer's model chip opens (webviews ModelPicker.tsx, QuickModelColumns.tsx; customize-app-profiles, the Claude Code app's model menu). list, the default: on a New Tab or a chat that can switch harness, the harness rail and its model columns with search. menu: the compact menu a started chat already opens (QuickModelMenu.tsx): the harness's numbered models, an Effort submenu and Fast mode where the harness has one, and More models for the full picker. A look turns it on.

help.text: List shows every harness and its models. Menu is a compact menu with the models, an Effort submenu and Fast mode.

rows.note: Whether the model menus' update footer (webviews harnessUpdateList.ts, HarnessUpdates.tsx) offers only the chat's own agent CLI. Off, the default: every outdated agent CLI on this Mac (Leo 2026-11-12, ask-3fdf0982ec). On: the chat's own update alone, as a one-agent app's model menu (customize-app-profiles: the Claude Code app lists no Codex update in a Claude chat). A look turns it on.

help.text: The model menu offers an update for this chat's agent only, not for every agent on this Mac.

rows.note: Whether a prompt sent while a turn runs waits in the queue (webviews queueing.ts; Leo, 2026-10-21, after ChatGPT's and Codex's "Turn off queueing"). A queued row's menu and the composer's button row write it; the agent pages' storage ends with the launch, so the pick lives here.

help.text: On, Send and ⌘Return queue a prompt sent while a turn runs, and Return steers it into the turn. Off, every send steers, so nothing waits.
Right-click the rail to move it.

rows.name: railShow
rows.note: What the prompt rail draws a tick for (webviews threadMinimap/railShow.ts; Leo, 2026-11-21: "why cant you see an agents'? why cant you filter it? customize it immediately?"). The rail's right-click menu and its head control write it too, so every rail changes at once.

help.text: Right-click the rail to change it.

rows.name: railControl
rows.note: A control at the prompt rail's head that names what it shows and opens the same choices (webviews threadMinimap/RailShowControl.tsx). Off by default: the rail looks as it did.

help.text: Shows what the rail lists above it while you point at it.

rows.note: How the chat's running tray names background commands no built-in rule knows (CommandLabelsSetting; webviews session-info/commandLabelSettings.ts): preset names and rules of one's own, edited as JSON.

help.text: The names the chat shows for background commands.

rows.page_hidden: a list of preset names and rule objects, edited in cmux-next.json

rows.name: layoutMessages
rows.note: Chat layout (structure a look reshapes; webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/chatLayout.ts sets it on the page root as a data attribute, chatLayout.css draws it). Hot-applies with the display event.

help.text: How your messages sit in the chat: a bubble on the right, a flat row on the left with an accent rule, or a card on the left.

rows.name: layoutComposer
rows.note: Chat layout (structure a look reshapes; webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/chatLayout.ts sets it on the page root as a data attribute, chatLayout.css draws it). Hot-applies with the display event.

help.text: The message box's outline: rounded, a pill, or square and docked.

rows.name: layoutHeader
rows.note: Chat layout (structure a look reshapes; webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/chatLayout.ts sets it on the page root as a data attribute, chatLayout.css draws it). Hot-applies with the display event.

help.text: Full shows the chat's header tools at all times; Quiet shows them only while the pointer is over the header.
